'''''Eugenia pyriformis''''' is a plant of the family [[Myrtaceae]] found primarily in [[Brazil]]. It reaches {{convert|6|to|13|m|ft}} in height and {{convert|30|to|50|cm|ft}} in trunk diameter. It is a native species of Brazil, occurring primarily in the states of [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], [[Rio Grande do Sul]], [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]] and [[São Paulo]].

==Cultivation==
It may grow at elevations of between {{convert|300|and|1500|m|ft}}. It requires a well drained, preferably slightly acid soil.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ecocrop.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/cropView?id=6002 |title=View crop<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2008-01-14 |archive-date=2019-08-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811204616/http://ecocrop.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/cropView%3Fid%3D6002 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Fruit==
''Eugenia pyriformis'' flowers between the months of August and December, and produces fruit between September and January. The yellow fruit of the plant is called ''uvalha'' and is edible.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.crfg.org/pubs/fl/commonSZ.html|title=Common Fruit Names - S-Z, California Rare Fruit Growers, Inc|access-date=2008-01-14|archive-date=2020-04-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200405135658/http://www.crfg.org/pubs/fl/commonSZ.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Some environmentalists have recommended use of the plant for projects of [[reforestation]] in Brazil, especially in degraded areas and permanent nature preserves.{{citation needed|date=January 2008}} The plant is also popular for ornamental or domestic purposes.
